# Command-line reference

Captured from `stabilis --help` and every subcommand's `--help`.
The library API is documented separately, in [api/index.md](api/index.md).

## Commands

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| [`stabilis docs`](#stabilis-docs) | read the theory pages |
| [`stabilis validate`](#stabilis-validate) | run the validation evidence report |
| [`stabilis stats`](#stabilis-stats) | basic statistics for a data file |
| [`stabilis adev`](#stabilis-adev) | Non-overlapping Allan deviation. See theory/avar.md. |
| [`stabilis oadev`](#stabilis-oadev) | Overlapping Allan deviation. See theory/avar.md. |
| [`stabilis mdev`](#stabilis-mdev) | Modified Allan deviation. See theory/mvar.md. |
| [`stabilis tdev`](#stabilis-tdev) | Time deviation, in seconds. See theory/tdev.md. |
| [`stabilis ohdev`](#stabilis-ohdev) | Overlapping Hadamard deviation. See theory/hvar.md. |
| [`stabilis totdev`](#stabilis-totdev) | Total deviation: TOTDEV, the square root of TOTVAR. |
| [`stabilis theo1`](#stabilis-theo1) | Thêo1 deviation, out to 75 % of the record length. |
| [`stabilis theobr`](#stabilis-theobr) | Bias-removed Thêo1, SP 1065 eq. (33). |
| [`stabilis theoh`](#stabilis-theoh) | ThêoH, SP 1065 eq. (34): AVAR at short tau, ThêoBR beyond it. |
| [`stabilis mtie`](#stabilis-mtie) | Maximum time interval error: the largest peak-to-peak in any window. |
| [`stabilis tierms`](#stabilis-tierms) | RMS time interval error over intervals of length tau. |
| [`stabilis wdev`](#stabilis-wdev) | Wavelet deviation on the **Allan scale**: `sqrt(2 * nu^2)`. |
| [`stabilis compare-edof`](#stabilis-compare-edof) | every EDOF method side by side, and what each does to the bounds |
| [`stabilis powerlaw`](#stabilis-powerlaw) | decompose sigma(tau) into IEEE 1139 h_alpha levels and drift |
| [`stabilis fit`](#stabilis-fit) | fit a model to a measured sigma-tau curve, with uncertainties that count the correlation between taus |
| [`stabilis cross`](#stabilis-cross) | cross-variance of two channels watching one clock, which rejects the instruments' own noise |
| [`stabilis reject`](#stabilis-reject) | average every pair of M channels watching one clock, which rejects instrument noise deeper than any single pair |
| [`stabilis plot`](#stabilis-plot) | plot a data file (needs matplotlib) |
| [`stabilis report`](#stabilis-report) | an HTML measurement report, with a conformity verdict that respects the error bars |
| [`stabilis gui`](#stabilis-gui) | a small local page in your browser, instead of flags |
| [`stabilis spur`](#stabilis-spur) | discrete tones: find them, measure them, optionally remove them and say so |
| [`stabilis mask`](#stabilis-mask) | judge a record against a limit mask, with the margin at the worst point |
| [`stabilis psd`](#stabilis-psd) | power spectral density, and L(f) where it is meaningful |
| [`stabilis davar`](#stabilis-davar) | dynamic stability: sigma(tau) as a function of when you looked |
| [`stabilis stream`](#stabilis-stream) | run the Allan deviation over a file as it is written |
| [`stabilis export`](#stabilis-export) | write data, curves and report bundles back out |
| [`stabilis export data`](#stabilis-export-data) | the record itself, in a format another tool can read |
| [`stabilis export table`](#stabilis-export-table) | the sigma-tau curve, for a spreadsheet, a program, or Stable32 |
| [`stabilis export bundle`](#stabilis-export-bundle) | a directory carrying the data, the curve, the report and a manifest of what everything hashes to |
| [`stabilis bench`](#stabilis-bench) | the measurement setup: what it can and cannot determine |
| [`stabilis bench check`](#stabilis-bench-check) | can this setup separate its oscillators? reads no data files |
| [`stabilis bench recommend`](#stabilis-bench-recommend) | which technique this setup supports -- hat, cross-correlation, or both -- and which assumption each answer rests on |
| [`stabilis bench solve`](#stabilis-bench-solve) | N-cornered hat and channel floors, one solve per tau |

---

## `stabilis`

```
usage: stabilis [-h] [--version] [--log-level {debug,info,warning,error}]
                {docs,validate,stats,adev,oadev,mdev,tdev,ohdev,totdev,theo1,theobr,theoh,mtie,tierms,wdev,compare-edof,powerlaw,fit,cross,reject,plot,report,gui,spur,mask,psd,davar,stream,export,bench}
                ...

Frequency stability analysis.

positional arguments:
  {docs,validate,stats,adev,oadev,mdev,tdev,ohdev,totdev,theo1,theobr,theoh,mtie,tierms,wdev,compare-edof,powerlaw,fit,cross,reject,plot,report,gui,spur,mask,psd,davar,stream,export,bench}
    docs                read the theory pages
    validate            run the validation evidence report
    stats               basic statistics for a data file
    adev                Non-overlapping Allan deviation. See theory/avar.md.
    oadev               Overlapping Allan deviation. See theory/avar.md.
    mdev                Modified Allan deviation. See theory/mvar.md.
    tdev                Time deviation, in seconds. See theory/tdev.md.
    ohdev               Overlapping Hadamard deviation. See theory/hvar.md.
    totdev              Total deviation: TOTDEV, the square root of TOTVAR.
    theo1               Thêo1 deviation, out to 75 % of the record length.
    theobr              Bias-removed Thêo1, SP 1065 eq. (33).
    theoh               ThêoH, SP 1065 eq. (34): AVAR at short tau, ThêoBR beyond it.
    mtie                Maximum time interval error: the largest peak-to-peak in any
                        window.
    tierms              RMS time interval error over intervals of length tau.
    wdev                Wavelet deviation on the **Allan scale**: `sqrt(2 * nu^2)`.
    compare-edof        every EDOF method side by side, and what each does to the
                        bounds
    powerlaw            decompose sigma(tau) into IEEE 1139 h_alpha levels and drift
    fit                 fit a model to a measured sigma-tau curve, with uncertainties
                        that count the correlation between taus
    cross               cross-variance of two channels watching one clock, which
                        rejects the instruments' own noise
    reject              average every pair of M channels watching one clock, which
                        rejects instrument noise deeper than any single pair
    plot                plot a data file (needs matplotlib)
    report              an HTML measurement report, with a conformity verdict that
                        respects the error bars
    gui                 a small local page in your browser, instead of flags
    spur                discrete tones: find them, measure them, optionally remove
                        them and say so
    mask                judge a record against a limit mask, with the margin at the
                        worst point
    psd                 power spectral density, and L(f) where it is meaningful
    davar               dynamic stability: sigma(tau) as a function of when you looked
    stream              run the Allan deviation over a file as it is written
    export              write data, curves and report bundles back out
    bench               the measurement setup: what it can and cannot determine

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit
  --log-level {debug,info,warning,error}
                        how much of the step log to print to stderr (default: warning)
```

## `stabilis docs`

Read the theory pages.

```
usage: stabilis docs [-h] [--list] [topic]

positional arguments:
  topic       topic name, e.g. noise-types

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --list      list all topics
```

## `stabilis validate`

Run the validation evidence report.

```
usage: stabilis validate [-h] [--out OUT] [--json] [--trials TRIALS] [--self-test]

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --out OUT        write an HTML report to this path
  --json           emit JSON to stdout
  --trials TRIALS  Monte-Carlo depth; raised to 300 if lower (default: 300, published
                   figures use 800)
  --self-test      inject a check designed to fail, proving the report can
```

## `stabilis stats`

Basic statistics for a data file.

```
usage: stabilis stats [-h] [--kind {phase,frequency}] [--rate RATE] [--column COLUMN]
                      [--time-column TIME_COLUMN] [--delimiter DELIMITER]
                      [--gap-value GAP_VALUE] [--json]
                      path

positional arguments:
  path                  input data file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --kind {phase,frequency}
                        whether the column holds phase in seconds or fractional
                        frequency
  --rate RATE           sample rate in Hz
  --column COLUMN       data column, 0-based
  --time-column TIME_COLUMN
                        timetag column, to infer --rate
  --delimiter DELIMITER
                        override delimiter sniffing
  --gap-value GAP_VALUE
                        value marking a gap (Stable32 writes 0; not assumed)
  --json                emit JSON
```

## `stabilis adev`

Non-overlapping allan deviation. see theory/avar.md..

```
usage: stabilis adev [-h] [--kind {phase,frequency}] [--rate RATE] [--column COLUMN]
                     [--time-column TIME_COLUMN] [--delimiter DELIMITER]
                     [--gap-value GAP_VALUE] [--taus {all,octave,decade,log}]
                     [--max-af MAX_AF] [--gap-policy {auto,mask,segment}]
                     [--confidence CONFIDENCE]
                     [--edof-method {auto,eta1,eta3,greenhall,totvar}]
                     [--alpha {2,1,0,-1,-2,-3,-4}] [--run-policy {pool,fallback}]
                     [--no-confidence] [--json]
                     path

positional arguments:
  path                  input data file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --kind {phase,frequency}
                        whether the column holds phase in seconds or fractional
                        frequency
  --rate RATE           sample rate in Hz
  --column COLUMN       data column, 0-based
  --time-column TIME_COLUMN
                        timetag column, to infer --rate
  --delimiter DELIMITER
                        override delimiter sniffing
  --gap-value GAP_VALUE
                        value marking a gap (Stable32 writes 0; not assumed)
  --taus {all,octave,decade,log}
                        tau grid
  --max-af MAX_AF       largest averaging factor
  --gap-policy {auto,mask,segment}
                        how a gap affects nearby terms; see `stabilis docs gaps`
  --confidence CONFIDENCE
                        confidence level for the sigma bounds (default: 1 sigma,
                        0.6827)
  --edof-method {auto,eta1,eta3,greenhall,totvar}
                        degrees-of-freedom estimator; see `stabilis docs edof`
  --alpha {2,1,0,-1,-2,-3,-4}
                        power law to assume, with --edof-method greenhall. Omit to
                        identify it per tau; pass Stable32's Alpha column to reproduce
                        one of its runs exactly. See `stabilis docs greenhall`
  --run-policy {pool,fallback}
                        on a gapped record, whether greenhall pools the runs or
                        declines to them (default: pool)
  --no-confidence       skip the bounds; also frees the coefficient arrays, which
                        matter on a record of millions of points
  --json                emit JSON
```

## `stabilis wdev`

Wavelet deviation on the **allan scale**: `sqrt(2 * nu^2)`..

```
usage: stabilis wdev [-h] [--kind {phase,frequency}] [--rate RATE] [--column COLUMN]
                     [--time-column TIME_COLUMN] [--delimiter DELIMITER]
                     [--gap-value GAP_VALUE] [--filter {d4,d6,d8,haar}]
                     [--levels LEVELS] [--biased] [--confidence CONFIDENCE]
                     [--edof-method {auto,eta1,eta3,greenhall,totvar}]
                     [--no-confidence] [--json]
                     path

positional arguments:
  path                  input data file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --kind {phase,frequency}
                        whether the column holds phase in seconds or fractional
                        frequency
  --rate RATE           sample rate in Hz
  --column COLUMN       data column, 0-based
  --time-column TIME_COLUMN
                        timetag column, to infer --rate
  --delimiter DELIMITER
                        override delimiter sniffing
  --gap-value GAP_VALUE
                        value marking a gap (Stable32 writes 0; not assumed)
  --filter {d4,d6,d8,haar}
                        wavelet family. haar (K=1) reproduces the overlapping ADEV
                        exactly; d4 (K=2) additionally annihilates a linear frequency
                        drift, d6 a quadratic, d8 a cubic
  --levels LEVELS       stop after this many octaves (default: as many as the record
                        supports)
  --biased              keep the coefficients that wrapped the circular boundary.
                        Shift-invariant and wrong: it treats the end of the record as
                        adjacent to its start
  --confidence CONFIDENCE
                        confidence level for the sigma bounds (default: 1 sigma)
  --edof-method {auto,eta1,eta3,greenhall,totvar}
                        degrees-of-freedom estimator; see `stabilis docs edof`
  --no-confidence       skip the bounds
  --json                emit JSON
```

## `stabilis fit`

Fit a model to a measured sigma-tau curve, with uncertainties that count the correlation between taus.

```
usage: stabilis fit [-h] [--kind {phase,frequency}] [--rate RATE] [--column COLUMN]
                    [--time-column TIME_COLUMN] [--delimiter DELIMITER]
                    [--gap-value GAP_VALUE] [--model MODEL]
                    [--estimator {adev,oadev,mdev,tdev,ohdev,totdev}]
                    [--taus {all,octave,decade,log}] [--max-af MAX_AF]
                    [--objective {ml,wlsq,logspace}] [--freeze NAME=VALUE]
                    [--bootstrap N] [--seed SEED] [--level LEVEL] [--json]
                    path

positional arguments:
  path                  input data file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --kind {phase,frequency}
                        whether the column holds phase in seconds or fractional
                        frequency
  --rate RATE           sample rate in Hz
  --column COLUMN       data column, 0-based
  --time-column TIME_COLUMN
                        timetag column, to infer --rate
  --delimiter DELIMITER
                        override delimiter sniffing
  --gap-value GAP_VALUE
                        value marking a gap (Stable32 writes 0; not assumed)
  --model MODEL         model name -- powerlaw, drift, gauss_markov, quantization,
                        bump, or a registered plugin. Use `stabilis powerlaw` instead
                        for the IEEE 1139 decomposition, which is an exact solve
                        rather than an optimization
  --estimator {adev,oadev,mdev,tdev,ohdev,totdev}
                        which curve to fit. A decimating estimator such as adev has no
                        measurable cross-tau correlation, so its error bars come back
                        as lower bounds
  --taus {all,octave,decade,log}
                        tau grid
  --max-af MAX_AF       largest averaging factor
  --objective {ml,wlsq,logspace}
                        'ml' is the exact chi-square likelihood; the others are for
                        comparability with tools that fit differently
  --freeze NAME=VALUE   hold a parameter at a value; repeatable
  --bootstrap N         resampled refits for a percentile interval (a typical run is
                        200); 0 skips it
  --seed SEED           seed for the bootstrap, so a report is reproducible
  --level LEVEL         confidence level (default: one sigma)
  --json                emit JSON
```

## `stabilis report`

An html measurement report, with a conformity verdict that respects the error bars.

```
usage: stabilis report [-h] [--kind {phase,frequency}] [--rate RATE] [--column COLUMN]
                       [--time-column TIME_COLUMN] [--delimiter DELIMITER]
                       [--gap-value GAP_VALUE]
                       [--estimator {adev,oadev,mdev,tdev,ohdev,totdev}]
                       [--taus {all,octave,decade,log}] [--max-af MAX_AF]
                       [--confidence CONFIDENCE] [--spec TAU:SIGMA] [--mask NAME]
                       [--bench BENCH] [--source SOURCE] [--title TITLE]
                       [--subject SUBJECT] [--operator OPERATOR] [--notes NOTES]
                       [--decompose] [--no-figure] [--out OUT] [--json]
                       path

positional arguments:
  path                  input data file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --kind {phase,frequency}
                        whether the column holds phase in seconds or fractional
                        frequency
  --rate RATE           sample rate in Hz
  --column COLUMN       data column, 0-based
  --time-column TIME_COLUMN
                        timetag column, to infer --rate
  --delimiter DELIMITER
                        override delimiter sniffing
  --gap-value GAP_VALUE
                        value marking a gap (Stable32 writes 0; not assumed)
  --estimator {adev,oadev,mdev,tdev,ohdev,totdev}
  --taus {all,octave,decade,log}
  --max-af MAX_AF       largest averaging factor
  --confidence CONFIDENCE
                        confidence level for every interval and for the verdict
  --spec TAU:SIGMA      one specification point, repeatable. The tau grid is extended
                        to hit each one exactly, so a limit is never interpolated
  --mask NAME           judge against a published limit too; repeatable, and `stabilis
                        mask --list-masks` shows the catalogue
  --bench BENCH         bench.json to read spec points from
  --source SOURCE       which source in --bench carries the specification
  --title TITLE
  --subject SUBJECT     what was measured
  --operator OPERATOR   who measured it
  --notes NOTES         conditions worth stating
  --decompose           include the power-law decomposition (adds an mdev pass)
  --no-figure           omit the plot; the report needs no matplotlib without it
  --out OUT             write HTML here (default: stdout)
  --json                emit JSON instead
```

```
                      [--time-column TIME_COLUMN] [--delimiter DELIMITER]
                      [--gap-value GAP_VALUE] --window WINDOW [--step STEP]
                      [--estimator ESTIMATOR] [--taus {all,octave,decade,log}]
                      [--max-af MAX_AF] [--level LEVEL] [--at-af AT_AF] [--json]

options:

                        frequency

  --delimiter DELIMITER
                        override delimiter sniffing

                        value marking a gap (Stable32 writes 0; not assumed)
  --window WINDOW       window length in SAMPLES; rounding a duration silently is how
                        two runs land on different grids

                        smallest)
```

## `stabilis stream`

Run the allan deviation over a file as it is written.

```
usage: stabilis stream [-h] --rate RATE [--af AF] [--taus {all,octave,decade,log}]
                       [--expect EXPECT] [--column COLUMN] [--time-column TIME_COLUMN]
                       [--delimiter DELIMITER] [--follow] [--timeout TIMEOUT]
                       [--every EVERY] [--json]
                       path

positional arguments:
  path                  file to read, or to follow with --follow

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --rate RATE           sample rate in Hz; a stream has no header to read it from
  --af AF               comma-separated averaging factors
  --taus {all,octave,decade,log}
                        with --expect, the grid to build (default: octave)
  --expect EXPECT       expected record length, to size the tau grid; a stream has no
                        length, so one of --af or --expect is required
  --column COLUMN
  --time-column TIME_COLUMN
                        timetag column; without one a dropped sample leaves no trace
                        and gaps are undetectable
  --delimiter DELIMITER
  --follow              keep reading as the file grows
  --timeout TIMEOUT     give up after this many seconds with no new data (default: 5)
  --every EVERY         print the running result every N samples
  --json
```

## `stabilis export data`

```
                            [--column COLUMN] [--time-column TIME_COLUMN]
                            [--delimiter DELIMITER] [--gap-value GAP_VALUE]
                            [--format {stabilis,csv,stable32}]
                            [--time-column-out {elapsed,unix,mjd}] [--gap-out VALUE]
                            [--digits DIGITS] --out OUT
                            path

positional arguments:
  path                  input data file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --kind {phase,frequency}
                        whether the column holds phase in seconds or fractional
                        frequency
  --rate RATE           sample rate in Hz
  --column COLUMN       data column, 0-based
  --time-column TIME_COLUMN
                        timetag column, to infer --rate
  --delimiter DELIMITER
                        override delimiter sniffing
  --gap-value GAP_VALUE
                        value marking a gap (Stable32 writes 0; not assumed)
  --format {stabilis,csv,stable32}
                        stabilis: a comment header carrying the rate and epoch, so
                        this library reads the series back whole. csv: the same,
                        comma-separated. stable32: bare numbers, no header, for
                        Stable32 and TimeLab
  --time-column-out {elapsed,unix,mjd}

  --digits DIGITS       significant digits (default 17, the width at which float64
                        reads back exactly)
```

```
                             [--estimator {adev,oadev,mdev,tdev,ohdev,totdev}]
                             [--taus {all,octave,decade,log}] [--max-af MAX_AF]
                             [--gap-policy {auto,mask,segment}]
                             [--confidence CONFIDENCE]
                             [--edof-method {auto,eta1,eta3,greenhall,totvar}]
                             [--alpha ALPHA] [--no-confidence]
                             [--format {csv,json,stable32}] [--out OUT]
                             path

positional arguments:
  path                  input data file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --kind {phase,frequency}
                        whether the column holds phase in seconds or fractional
                        frequency
  --rate RATE           sample rate in Hz
  --column COLUMN       data column, 0-based
  --time-column TIME_COLUMN
                        timetag column, to infer --rate
  --delimiter DELIMITER
                        override delimiter sniffing
  --gap-value GAP_VALUE
                        value marking a gap (Stable32 writes 0; not assumed)
  --estimator {adev,oadev,mdev,tdev,ohdev,totdev}
  --taus {all,octave,decade,log}
  --max-af MAX_AF       largest averaging factor
  --gap-policy {auto,mask,segment}
  --confidence CONFIDENCE
  --edof-method {auto,eta1,eta3,greenhall,totvar}
  --alpha ALPHA         assumed power law; required by --format stable32 unless the
                        interval already carries one
  --no-confidence       curve only, no interval
  --format {csv,json,stable32}
                        csv: eight columns for a spreadsheet. json: every field,
                        including what the csv cannot carry. stable32: the block
                        Stable32 prints, to its own bytes -- and to its four decimals
  --out OUT             write here (default: stdout)
```

## `stabilis export bundle`

A directory carrying the data, the curve, the report and a manifest of what everything hashes to.

```
usage: stabilis export bundle [-h] [--kind {phase,frequency}] [--rate RATE]
                              [--column COLUMN] [--time-column TIME_COLUMN]
                              [--delimiter DELIMITER] [--gap-value GAP_VALUE]
                              [--estimator {adev,oadev,mdev,tdev,ohdev,totdev}]
                              [--taus {all,octave,decade,log}] [--max-af MAX_AF]
                              [--gap-policy {auto,mask,segment}]
                              [--confidence CONFIDENCE]
                              [--edof-method {auto,eta1,eta3,greenhall,totvar}]
                              [--alpha ALPHA] [--spec TAU:SIGMA] [--bench BENCH]
                              [--source SOURCE] [--title TITLE] [--subject SUBJECT]
                              [--operator OPERATOR] [--notes NOTES] [--no-data]
                              [--no-figure] [--no-stamp] [--overwrite] --out DIR
                              path

positional arguments:
  path                  input data file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --kind {phase,frequency}
                        whether the column holds phase in seconds or fractional
                        frequency
  --rate RATE           sample rate in Hz
  --column COLUMN       data column, 0-based
  --time-column TIME_COLUMN
                        timetag column, to infer --rate
  --delimiter DELIMITER
                        override delimiter sniffing
  --gap-value GAP_VALUE
                        value marking a gap (Stable32 writes 0; not assumed)
  --estimator {adev,oadev,mdev,tdev,ohdev,totdev}
  --taus {all,octave,decade,log}
  --max-af MAX_AF       largest averaging factor
  --gap-policy {auto,mask,segment}
  --confidence CONFIDENCE
  --edof-method {auto,eta1,eta3,greenhall,totvar}
  --alpha ALPHA         assumed power law
  --spec TAU:SIGMA      a datasheet limit, repeatable
  --bench BENCH         bench.json, to take the limits from
  --source SOURCE       which oscillator in --bench
  --title TITLE
  --subject SUBJECT
  --operator OPERATOR
  --notes NOTES
  --no-data             reference the source record by hash instead of copying it in
  --no-figure
  --no-stamp            omit the creation time, so two bundles of the same analysis
                        are byte-identical
  --overwrite           write over a directory that already holds one
  --out DIR
```

## `stabilis bench`

The measurement setup: what it can and cannot determine.

```
usage: stabilis bench [-h] {check,recommend,solve} ...

positional arguments:
  {check,recommend,solve}
    check               can this setup separate its oscillators? reads no data files
    recommend           which technique this setup supports -- hat, cross-correlation,
                        or both -- and which assumption each answer rests on
    solve               N-cornered hat and channel floors, one solve per tau

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
```

## `stabilis bench check`

Can this setup separate its oscillators? reads no data files.

```
usage: stabilis bench check [-h] [--json] path

positional arguments:
  path        bench.json

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      emit JSON
```

## `stabilis bench recommend`

Which technique this setup supports -- hat, cross-correlation, or both -- and which assumption each answer rests on.

```
usage: stabilis bench recommend [-h] [--json] path

positional arguments:
  path        bench.json

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      emit JSON
```

## `stabilis bench solve`

N-cornered hat and channel floors, one solve per tau.

```
usage: stabilis bench solve [-h] [--estimator {adev,oadev,mdev,tdev,ohdev,totdev}]
                            [--taus {all,octave,decade,log}] [--max-af MAX_AF]
                            [--allow-unidentifiable] [--no-verify] [--json]
                            path

positional arguments:
  path                  bench.json

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --estimator {adev,oadev,mdev,tdev,ohdev,totdev}
  --taus {all,octave,decade,log}
  --max-af MAX_AF       largest averaging factor
  --allow-unidentifiable
                        solve a singular bench anyway; the answer is then one of
                        infinitely many that fit equally well
  --no-verify           skip the SHA-256 check on the referenced data files
  --json                emit JSON
```
